title: I Enforced the Trampoline-Park Grip-Sock Rule on the Manager's Kids

parts.text: I scanned tickets at 10:11 a.m. and two kids hopped the court in street socks. The grip-sock rule the manager posted said: GRIP SOCKS ON COURT. NO EXCEPTIONS FOR STAFF FAMILIES. I was twenty-four, weekend cashier, holding a bin of unsold pairs. Manager Dale said, "My kids know the foam." I pointed at his poster. He waved. "Management is the foam." I photographed the street socks, the poster, and the waiver clipboard. Then I paused their bands at the gate until socks rang up. At 10:16 the regional asked why Dale's name was on a sock-waiver ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Regional can see street socks on court against the poster Dale posted.

social.video_title: The manager's kids skipped the grip socks — Part 1/2
social.description: Court gate, street socks, and a poster about staff families. I paused the bands. Would you have sold the pair?

parts.text: Dale called it a demo until the waiver desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the poster, and the still. The kids bought grips. Dale told the staff the poster was always about optics. Optics is a word managers use when foam meets a camera. Sock policy now has a second line: MANAGEMENT IS NOT THE FOAM. I keep the bin by the gate. Dale's kids ring up. The court finally grips.

social.video_title: Management is not the foam — Part 2/2
social.description: Waiver ticket, purchased grips, and a second line on the poster. Was knowing the foam ever a skip?
